description: Frozen, evidence-corrected claim-kind, source-disposition and ledger-value vocabulary for documentation authority unification. Version 1 meanings are kept; version 2 adds the values the inventory actually emits.

evidence.method: Distinct values counted over the 86,085 claimLedger rows and 4,311 inventory items of the regenerated inventory (scripts/generate-doc-inventory.mjs); generator-only values read from the generator source.

changesFromV1.evidence: 10,826 claim rows and 4,252 of 4,311 files emit it; scripts/check-doc-inventory-gates.mjs adds it to the vocabulary by hand (claimKinds.add).

v1 named four classes only inside allowedFileClasses; the inventory emits a fifth for 14 files (docs/templates/**, docs/architecture-manifest.json, docs/doc-registry.json, docs/user/README.md), and the gates checker keeps a private four-class list. unknown-blocking therefore also allows the new class.

changesFromV1.change: add authorityKinds, claimStatuses, reviewStatuses, corpora, relationTypes and identityStatuses sections
changesFromV1.evidence: plan §6.2 requires these ledger fields but v1 defined no values; the inventory emits legacy-current, candidate, promoted, non-authority, unclassified; current, future, historical; blocking, pending; four corpora; one relation type; two identity statuses.

changesFromV1.change: mark ten dispositions "reserved" (move, split, extract, redirect, supersede, archive-with-reason, delete-as-duplicate, delete-as-obsolete, defer-with-owner, reject-with-rationale)
changesFromV1.evidence: No inventory item and no ledger row uses them yet; they are assigned by the transformation phases. Meanings are unchanged.

changesFromV1.change: add reviewStatus "reviewed" as the reserved terminal value and "needs-review" as the carry-forward marker
changesFromV1.evidence: The ledger only holds blocking and pending; the identity registry marks 122 edited units needs-review (generate-doc-inventory.mjs carry-forward). A review phase needs a closing value.

changesFromV1.change: correct the documented ledger-field count from 14 to 15 (Markdown only)
changesFromV1.evidence: minimumLedgerFields in v1 lists 15 names; the Markdown said "14 ledger fields".

changesFromV1.change: record per-value usage (in-use, reserved, generator-only) and keep value definitions unchanged
changesFromV1.evidence: Plan §6.3 requires every emitted value to be defined and every unused one flagged.

changesFromV1.change: authorityClasses section added by additive amendment v2.1-001

sourceDispositions.definition: Source content moves into the target docs/platform/** structure as the sole maintained canonical authority.
Source file moves directly to target structure with minimal structural rewrite, becoming the canonical owner.
Content from multiple sources is combined into a single canonical target document.
Source is partitioned into multiple target documents, with complete claim-level tracking for every section and block.
Specific claims, contracts, or sections are extracted from a larger file into a dedicated target document.
Source is replaced with an explicit read-only pointer or stub referencing the canonical target; retains no substantive claims.
Source is preserved as immutable historical evidence, test fixture, or audit receipt; never serves as default reading authority.
File is a machine-readable derived projection generated automatically from underlying source truth, code, or events.
File belongs to a distinct non-platform corpus (e.g., user-facing knowledge docs, domains, or tutorials) and is governed outside platform authority.
Source or claim has been explicitly superseded by a newer approved decision or architecture, and is retired.
Source is retired and relocated to history/archive with an explicit, durable justification recorded in the ledger.
Source is an unneeded exact or semantic duplicate of another document and will be safely removed at cutover without alias.
Source is completely obsolete and retains zero evidentiary, contractual, or historical value; deleted at cutover.
Source or claim is deliberately deferred to a named future phase or engine, with a named owner and revisit trigger.
Source proposal or candidate design was evaluated and formally rejected with durable rationale.
Source status, claims, or consumers are unresolved; blocks cutover until audited and assigned a definitive disposition.

claimKinds.description: Immutable platform axioms, operating laws (L1–L8), and constitutional rules.
Normative schema, protocol, interface invariant, boundary obligation, or handoff rule.
Observable current behavior, state model, operations, shared entities, and lifecycle transitions.
System or component topology, design rationale, boundary definition, and trade-off analysis.
Architectural or product choice, problem statement, options evaluated, rationale, and supersession links.
High-level mission, long-horizon intended direction, scope, and explicit non-scope.
Preserved design intent across simplified implementation slices, must-not-preclude constraints, and revisit triggers.
Supported operator procedure, runbook, or maintenance instructions.
Empirical proof, test suite receipt, benchmark output, or verification record supporting a claim.
Provenance, historical milestone, retrospective observation, or retired context.
Area portal, subcomponent map, reading map, or index routing readers to canonical documents.
Placeholder for a claim unit the inventory could not yet classify. Never a final value: every row with this kind must be re-kinded before conservation can close.

fileClasses.definition: Maintained prose that may establish authority for a claim.
Maintained source prose kept only until its claims are carried to a canonical owner or retired.
Non-authority evidence, proof payloads, reports and archived context.
Derived projection that never outranks its source.
File with no switchboard route; only unknown-blocking is allowed until an area assigns a class.

corpora.definition: Platform documentation in scope of the authority migration.
End-user knowledge corpus governed by the knowledge registry; out of platform authority.
History and evidence corpus; never default reading authority.
Material owned by consumer projects (for example the distillery); out of platform authority.

authorityKinds.definition: Current authority still living in a legacy root or root document until superseded.
Target material under docs/platform/** that is not yet canonical.
Target material already declared the canonical owner by the switchboard.
Evidence, history or generated output that establishes no claim.
No switchboard route yet; blocks cutover.

claimStatuses.definition: The claim describes what is true now.
The claim describes intended or planned state.
The claim describes retired, past or evidentiary state.

reviewStatuses.definition: Disposition is unknown-blocking or identity is ambiguous; blocks cutover.
Proposed disposition exists and awaits review.
A named reviewer accepted the disposition, owner and target anchor.
Carry-forward marker for a unit edited since it was last reviewed; lives in the identity registry.

relationTypes.definition: The claim shares identical content with other source paths (one semantic claim, several occurrences).
Identical units inside one file that carry-forward could not pair; blocks until paired by anchor.

identityStatuses.definition: Identity carried from the committed registry.
Several registry rows could match; identity is a blocking gap.
Identical duplicate units that could not be paired.
No registry row matches the unit.
Source identity conflicts between registry documents.

amendmentRule: Version 2 is frozen for the meaning of every existing value. A new value or section is added only as an additive amendment (version 2.1, 2.2, ...) recorded in amendments with its evidence; the validator is re-run and the constitution keeps pinning the major version. Changing or removing an existing value needs a new major version and an owner decision.

amendments.change: add section authorityClasses and the class verification-record for the canonical verification kind
amendments.evidence: Naming the canonical verification kind's class evidence collided with the locked rule that evidence is not authority (plan §3 item 10). The class evidence now belongs only to non-authority kinds (evidence-payload, history); verification is canonical and becomes verification-record. Owner decision 2026-10-06.

amendments.change: move the dispositions split, supersede, archive-with-reason and delete-as-obsolete and the review status reviewed from usage reserved to usage in-use; no value, definition or rule text changes
amendments.evidence: Used by the dual pilot (2026-10-07): the 966 decision rows (600 of the host-invocation audit, 366 of the work-state transformation) of the shards under plans/260925-documentation-authority-unification/pilot/decisions/ carry split (6 rows), supersede (196), archive-with-reason (20) and delete-as-obsolete (7) next to promote (361), merge (149) and unknown-blocking (227); all 366 rows of the work-state sources carry reviewStatus reviewed with a reviewer and a date, accepted by scripts/check-doc-inventory-gates.mjs --decisions --strict --scope. move, extract, redirect, delete-as-duplicate, defer-with-owner and reject-with-rationale were not used and stay reserved.

authorityClasses.definition: Routes readers; establishes no claim of its own.
States the intended direction, scope and non-scope.
Preserves intent across simplified implementation slices.
Establishes exact obligations, laws and invariants.
Establishes boundaries, responsibilities and design rationale.
Records what was decided, why, and supersession.
Canonical record that proves or tracks a claim, contract, behavior or decision; owned by its area verification index.
Non-authority material: proof payloads and history. Evidence is not authority (plan §3 item 10).
Temporary read-only pointer to a canonical target.
